# buf.breaking compares against a Git tag: an added field passes, a deleted
# one fails, and moving the tag reruns the check with no file changed.
[!exec:buf] skip
[!exec:git] skip

exec git init -q
exec git add .
exec git -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=Test commit -qm base
exec git tag base

bit
stdout 'breaking ▶ buf breaking --against \.git#tag=base'
stdout 'breaking ✔ ok'

bit
stdout 'breaking · no changes'

cp user.proto.added proto/acme/v1/user.proto
bit
stdout 'breaking ✔ ok'

exec git -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=Test commit -qam 'add phone'
exec git tag -f base
bit
stdout 'baseline moved'
stdout 'breaking ✔ ok'

cp user.proto.deleted proto/acme/v1/user.proto
! bit
stdout 'Previously present field "3" with name "phone" on message "User" was deleted'
stdout 'breaking ✘ tests failed'

-- BUILD.bit --
breaking = buf.breaking {
  against = ".git#tag=base"
}
-- buf.yaml --
version: v2
modules:
  - path: proto
breaking:
  use:
    - FILE
-- proto/acme/v1/user.proto --
syntax = "proto3";

package acme.v1;

message User {
  string name = 1;
  string email = 2;
}
-- user.proto.added --
syntax = "proto3";

package acme.v1;

message User {
  string name = 1;
  string email = 2;
  string phone = 3;
}
-- user.proto.deleted --
syntax = "proto3";

package acme.v1;

message User {
  string name = 1;
  string email = 2;
}
